subject: Q2 OKR postmortem: scores, narrative points, and decision log
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 OKR postmortem: initial scores and ask

Team — attaching my consolidated score workbook and a set of raw notes from the retrospective. High level ask before Friday: please review the scores in the worksheet and the two narrative bullets per objective (column D) and reply with any score adjustments + short supporting sentence (why change).

Context in brief: overall achievement came in at ~78% weighted. We hit Delivery and Reliability targets ahead of plan, but growth funnel and enablement fell short. There are three decisions we need to lock this week for Q3 planning: (1) whether to reweight Objective 2 (Growth) from 30% to 25% and move 5% to Objective 4 (Platform Performance); (2) whether to extend the Acme pilot by 60 days to gather more telemetry; (3) a small headcount carve (0.4 FTE hiring deferral) in Growth engineering.

Please annotate the sheet directly where you disagree and add any proposed language to the narrative doc. Ill synthesize for the QBR deck and the exec summary.

Attachments: Q2_OKR_scores_v2.xlsx (worksheet with raw scores), Q2_retrospective_notes.docx (raw verbatim notes + grouped themes)

Thanks — t

Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>; Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-13T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 OKR postmortem: initial scores and ask

Thanks, Tessa — reviewed the sheet and left three inline comments. My quick notes:

- Objective 1 (Reliability): happy to keep 95% achievement at the credit. The incident MTTR improvements were real and materially reduced customer escalations.
- Objective 2 (Growth): I think the raw numbers understate the qualitative gains from the new developer onboarding flow. Recommend moving score from 62 -> 68 (scores are 0-100) but support the 25% weight idea. Rationale: conversions improved in experimental cohort and the lift is durable if we prioritize the follow-up automation work in Q3.
- Objective 3 (Cost per token): suggest lowering score to 70 (from 78) because we missed the target on edge-case inference paths where the KV cache warmed poorly.

On decisions: Im +1 on extending the Acme pilot 60 days to ensure we get a representative mix of long-tail workloads. We should attach a short appendix to the pilot with the telemetry schema so procurement signs off.

I added a narrative sentence for Objective 2 in the notion doc: "Growth progress reflects early wins from onboarding experiments; sustaining the lift requires automation of prompt-routing and investing 0.4 FTE in platform glue — otherwise the conversion delta will decay."

Vivek

Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-14T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 OKR postmortem: initial scores and ask

Good synthesis, Tessa — I reviewed and made the following editorial and substantive suggestions in the narrative doc:

1) For the exec summary, call out tradeoffs explicitly: we made a deliberate choice to prioritize reliability and Dedicated capacity during Q2 which constrained some growth experiments. Framing this as a tradeoff helps with stakeholder expectations.
2) For Objective 4 (Platform Performance), please add a line noting the kernel-level optimizations that reduced median latency by 12ms — thats a tangible engineering win worth highlighting.
3) For the proposed reweighting, recommend we model a 3-month runway (instead of a permanent weight change) and call it a "Q3 transitional reweight" so teams know this is tactical, not permanent.

Score edits: I accept Vivek's adjustment for Objective 2 (68). Also suggest we mark Objective 5 (Talent & Org) as "partial" with 55 — hiring slippage in Growth and CS hurt overall readiness.

Small nit: please remove the internal ticket IDs in the narrative doc for the public QBR version.

Laura

Date: 2026-08-14T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q2 OKR postmortem: initial scores and ask

Adding two operational observations from engineering:

- The KV cache hit improvement (Objective 3 work) disproportionately helped long-tail requests; that said, our load tests show a regression under 95th percentile burst scenarios — I left a comment and a suggested follow-up experiment (A/B routing policy tweak) in the sheet.
- On the Acme extension: engineering is neutral but requests that any extension include a clear on/off rollback criterion tied to API error rate and a monthly telemetry snapshot so we can cut the pilot early if strain increases.

I also flagged one item to move to the decision log: agree to defer 0.4 FTE hiring in Growth for one quarter (Q3), not permanently. Marcus will own documenting the exact scope that gets deferred.

M

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Ramos <jill.ramos@acme.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T17:41:00-07:00
Subject: Q2 OKR postmortem — final decisions and consolidated narrative (for QBR)

Thanks all for fast turns. Quick decision log below (finalized at 17:30 PT):

- Weighting: approve a Q3 transitional reweighting. Objective 2 (Growth) moves from 30% -> 25% for Q3; Objective 4 (Platform Performance) moves +5% for Q3. We will revisit at end of Q3. (owner: Tessa)
- Scores: apply the agreed individual score edits (Vivek's +6 on Obj2, Laura's Talent adjustment to 55, Marcus's cost tweak). Final weighted achievement = 76.4%. (owner: Tessa)
- Acme pilot: extend +60 days with telemetry appendix. Trigger: if API 5xx rate > 0.5% for two consecutive days, pilot auto-pauses and we notify procurement & ACME. (owner: Marcus to confirm telemetry schema; owners: Marcus + Jill)
- Hiring: defer 0.4 FTE Growth hiring for one quarter; scope to be documented in decision-log.csv. (owner: Marcus)
- QBR narrative: Ive merged the language into the notion doc and created a one-page exec summary focused on tradeoffs and next steps. Link above. (owner: Laura for editorial pass)

Next steps for this thread: please review the attached decision-log.csv and the updated worksheet. If no objections by 48 hours, I will mark this file as final and copy the exec summary into the QBR deck.

Attachments: decision-log.csv (decision table), Q2_OKR_scores_v2.xlsx (finalized), Q2_retrospective_notes.docx (redacted public version)

Thanks — t

Tessa Morgan
